To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 4-1BBligand is not required for the suppression of EAU by anti-4-lBB mAb and that 4-1-lBB-mediated suppression of uveitis is caused by IDO-dependent mechanisms.
the 4-1BBligand (4-18BBL)-mediated expansion of novel CD8+ T cells results in a high level of IDO expression in CD11c dendritic cells and suppresses EAU via IDO-dependent mechanisms.
cross-linking 4-1BBl on CD8+ T cells results in the generation of CD11c + CD8 + T cells that suppress EAU via IDO-dependent mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism of 4- 1BB-mediated suppression in autoimmune diseases.
the development and characterization of a new immunosuppressive therapy for the treatment of autoimmune diseases, including autoimmune uveitis, that is mediated by the 4-1BBligand and IDO.
understanding the role of 4- 1BB in regulating immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4-1BBlg-4-1BBr interaction plays a crucial role in the induction and suppression of experimental autoimmune uvetitis.
the 4-1BBl/4-1 BB interaction has an important role in the regulation of autoimmune diseases, including EAU.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-4-IBB mAb induces a population of novel CD8+ T cells with suppressive function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system has a mechanism to suppress autoimmunity.
cross-linking 4-1BBl on CD4+ T helper cells can lead to the expansion of a novel population of CD11c(+)CD8(+) T cells that can suppress the development of experimental autoimmune uvetis.
4-1BBlg/4-1 BB interaction is not essential for suppression of EAU, but rather that cross-linking 4-1 BB on T cells induces a novel population of CD8+ T cells to suppress EAU.
